findings.source_evidence: The source requires independent and identically distributed random variables and almost-sure convergence to their expectation.
findings.lean_evidence: IdentDistrib is supplied only as an opaque inductive declaration; IndepFun delegates to unsupplied Kernel.IndepFun; ae delegates to unsupplied filter machinery; nhds has body wrapped✝.1; integral is not semantically transparent at the supplied boundary.
findings.impact: The central hypotheses, convergence mode, and limit value cannot be compared without guessing imported semantics, so direct acceptance is impossible.

findings.source_evidence: The theorem is stated for random variables on a probability space.

findings.impact: This may be a legitimate strengthening, but it changes the quantified domain and is material until the relevant measure-dependent semantics are adjudicated.

findings.source_evidence: The source says i.i.d., conventionally including joint independence of the sequence.

findings.source_evidence: The source uses X₁ through X_N and positive N.
findings.lean_evidence: The target uses X 0 through X (n-1) and includes a defined n=0 sequence value.
findings.impact: This is ordinarily harmless zero-based reindexing because a finite initial term does not affect an atTop limit, but exact filter semantics remain part of adjudication.

rationale: The readable source contract and target syntax align on an infinite real sequence, finite first moment, normalized partial sums, the common-mean limit, almost-everywhere form, and absence of a variance assumption. The target also appears to strengthen the source by using pairwise independence and omitting a probability-measure restriction. Nevertheless, several material imported declarations are opaque at the supplied semantic boundary, especially IdentDistrib, IndepFun, ae, integral, and nhds. Following the instruction not to guess opaque imported semantics, both implication directions and the final faithfulness class remain undetermined and require adjudication.
